comparator.sourceNotes: The current 53-page OER Appendix 3, printed pp.34–36, explicitly applies the renewed programme to students starting in 2025–2026. Dutch first-year study and the neutrally selected International Economics and Policy route supply 180 documented EC. Article 17 permits approved, non-overlapping university study in the 24-EC choice space; this is not an unrestricted guarantee. Appendix 4, printed p.39, retains Academic Skills and OIM-A/MRI plus statistics entry requirements for the thesis, without an explicit renewed-course equivalence. No 2026-entry future-year programme, waiver or formal thesis eligibility is certified.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest UCR response retains economic theory, finance, business and quantitative research. The second route shifts five substantive courses toward economic policy, responsible firms and sustainability. Both remain feasible and differ by five courses each. Separate specialist finance and accounting routes are evidenced but cannot form credible distinct 24-course programmes from the current UCR offer without weak substitutes.

notes.text: Radboud provides a dedicated multi-year economics and business economics curriculum with a named specialisation, staged econometrics and a required economics thesis. UCR combines economics, business, quantitative research, policy and sustainability but does not reproduce that disciplinary depth or mandatory thesis. Radboud also permits 24 EC of free choice in year three.

audience.programmeDescription: The Dutch-language variant studies economic choices, firms, financial markets and policy. Its first-year curriculum is taught in Dutch; the illustrated International Economics and Policy route continues the shared economic and quantitative subjects. This renewed curriculum is explicitly illustrated for students who entered in 2025–2026.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The confirmed economics and business-economics curriculum supports two meaningful UCR responses: quantitative economics/business study and economic policy with responsible business and sustainability. UCR offers less specialist economics, finance and accounting depth and does not reproduce the staged econometrics sequence or required economics thesis. The unresolved thesis-entry rules prevent certification of the external pathway.

curriculum.limitation: The published components total 180 EC. The current thesis-entry table uses earlier methods-course names that have not been formally reconciled with the renewed curriculum. Thesis eligibility and old/new course equivalence are not verified.

componentNotes.y3-electives: 24 EC of approved choice, normally 18 EC in period 1 and 6 EC in period 4. Courses outside the programme require approval and must not overlap. Master’s and applied-science courses are normally excluded; exceptions for study abroad follow the learning agreement. An optional 12 EC internship may replace two 6 EC electives.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: Required 12 EC economics research project. The formal entry rule names earlier methods courses whose relationship to the renewed curriculum needs authoritative clarification.
componentNotes.y1-academic: Academic and professional skills are compulsory. The linked academic-language test adds no credits. First-year study advice normally requires 42 of 60 EC, subject to personal circumstances.

comparisonScope.excluded: Certification of thesis eligibility, earlier/new methods-course equivalence, waivers and a complete formally verified external progression pathway.

acceptance.claim: The confirmed economics and business-economics curriculum supports two meaningful UCR responses: quantitative economics/business study and economic policy with responsible business and sustainability.

acceptance.challengeMethod: Separately identified source-first second pass by the same AI reviewer against the official OER, current UCR evidence and exact finished inputs; no independent human or separate-agent review.

uncertainties.fact: The published components total 180 EC. The current thesis-entry table uses earlier methods-course names that have not been formally reconciled with the renewed curriculum. Thesis eligibility and old/new course equivalence are not verified.
